items.followUp: What is the role of light in the photolysis of water during photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Checks that photolysis is the light-driven splitting of water and that oxygen is produced.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that light splits water molecules and mentioning oxygen as a product.

rubric.why: Checks for the other products of water splitting used in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen ions/protons and electrons are produced and used in photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Photolysis of water is the splitting of water molecules by light energy during photosynthesis.
It produces oxygen, hydrogen ions (protons) and electrons; oxygen is released, while the hydrogen ions and electrons are used in photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Name four careers related to the study of biology and briefly explain one of them.

rubric.why: Recognises a biological career in medicine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming medicine, a doctor or physician as a profession and indicating that it involves diagnosing or treating disease.

rubric.why: Recognises the application of biology in crop production and farming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming agriculture/agriculturist and linking it to crops or farming.

rubric.why: Recognises a biological career concerned with forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming forestry/a forester and linking it to the care or management of forests.

rubric.why: Recognises a biological career involving fish and other aquatic resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming fisheries/aquaculture and linking it to fish breeding, farming or management.

modelAnswer: Medicine: doctors use biological knowledge to diagnose and treat diseases in humans.
Agriculture: agriculturists apply biology to improve crops and farming practices.
Forestry: foresters manage and conserve forests and forest resources.
Fisheries: fisheries experts breed, farm and manage fish and other aquatic organisms.

items.followUp: Draw and label a plant cell, showing at least six structures.

rubric.why: Checks for a recognisable plant-cell outline and its characteristic structures.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for a clear plant-cell diagram with a cell wall and at least one other correctly shown plant-cell structure.

rubric.why: Checks accurate labelling of two cell structures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correctly labelled structures from the model answer.

rubric.why: Checks for additional correctly labelled structures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two further correctly labelled structures, beyond those credited in the previous label point.

modelAnswer: Draw a large, roughly rectangular plant cell with a thick outer boundary for the cell wall.
Draw a thin cell membrane just inside the cell wall, and show cytoplasm filling the cell.
Draw a large central vacuole; place the nucleus, several chloroplasts and mitochondria in the cytoplasm.
Label at least six parts with clear label lines: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chloroplast, vacuole and mitochondrion.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature and pH affect the activity of enzymes.

rubric.why: Checks the rise in enzyme activity as temperature approaches its optimum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzyme activity increases with temperature up to an optimum.

rubric.why: Checks that high temperature changes enzyme structure and reduces activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that high temperature denatures the enzyme or changes its active site, so activity falls.

rubric.why: Checks that enzymes work best at a particular pH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each enzyme has an optimum pH at which its activity is highest.

rubric.why: Checks that pH changes away from the optimum reduce enzyme function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that unsuitable pH alters the active site or denatures the enzyme, lowering its activity.

modelAnswer: As temperature rises, enzyme activity increases until the enzyme reaches its optimum temperature.
Above the optimum, the enzyme may be denatured: its active site changes shape and the rate of reaction falls.
Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it works fastest.
A pH above or below this optimum changes the enzyme's structure or active site, reducing its activity; extreme pH may denature it.

items.followUp: Describe inhalation and exhalation, including the movements of the diaphragm and ribs.

rubric.why: Checks the muscle and rib movements that bring about inhalation.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for describing the diaphragm contracting and flattening, and the ribs moving up and out.

rubric.why: Checks the pressure and volume change that draws air into the lungs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chest volume increases, pressure decreases and air enters the lungs.

rubric.why: Checks the reverse movements during exhalation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the diaphragm relaxing and doming upward, and/or the ribs moving down and in.

rubric.why: Checks the pressure change that moves air out of the lungs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chest volume decreases, pressure increases and air is forced out.

modelAnswer: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, while the external intercostal muscles contract and move the ribs up and out.
The volume of the chest cavity increases and its pressure decreases, so air enters the lungs.
During exhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and becomes dome-shaped, while the ribs move down and in as the intercostal muscles relax.
The volume of the chest cavity decreases and its pressure increases, forcing air out of the lungs.

items.followUp: What are dietary fibres, and how do they help maintain a healthy digestive system?

rubric.why: Checks the source or identity of dietary fibre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fibre/roughage as indigestible plant material, such as cellulose.

rubric.why: Checks that fibre is not broken down and absorbed as ordinary food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that dietary fibre is not digested by human digestive enzymes.

rubric.why: Checks how fibre adds bulk and retains water in waste.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that fibre adds bulk to faeces/stool or helps it retain water.

rubric.why: Checks the benefit to movement of food and prevention of constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fibre promotes peristalsis or helps prevent constipation.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibres, also called roughage, are the indigestible parts of plant foods, such as cellulose.
They are not digested by human digestive enzymes.
Fibre absorbs and holds water and adds bulk to the faeces.
This helps peristalsis move material through the gut and prevents constipation.

items.followUp: Compare the structure and function of arteries, veins and capillaries.

rubric.why: Checks the number and names of the main blood-vessel types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming arteries, veins and capillaries as the three types of blood vessels.

rubric.why: Checks the direction in which arteries carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that arteries carry blood away from the heart.

rubric.why: Checks the characteristic artery wall that withstands high pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing artery walls as thick, muscular and/or elastic.

rubric.why: Checks the direction in which veins carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that veins carry blood toward the heart.

rubric.why: Checks vein structure and how valves help blood return to the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing veins as having thinner walls, a wider lumen or valves that prevent backflow.

modelAnswer: There are three types of blood vessels: arteries, veins and capillaries.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Their walls are thick, muscular and elastic to withstand the high pressure of blood.
Veins carry blood toward the heart. Their walls are thinner than those of arteries and they have a wider lumen.
Veins contain valves that prevent the backflow of blood.

items.followUp: State one use of biotechnology in agriculture or medicine.

rubric.why: Checks that biotechnology involves applying technology to living organisms or biological systems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining biotechnology as the use or application of organisms, cells or biological processes.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of biotechnology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that this application produces useful products or services for humans.

modelAnswer: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells or biological processes to make useful products or provide services for humans.
